title: decisions query side (active, search, archive, tag) — renderer split out to rpl-10
action: Port the decisions QUERY verbs only: active, search, archive, tag (lib at packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:739 archiveDecisions, :810 the active projection; handlers in packages/bee/bee.mjs:1924-2229). The index renderer and its --check drift verdict were SPLIT OUT into rpl-10 on review (this cell was over the plan's own reference size). archive and tag are read-modify-write and take the same D9 lock as the write path — consume crates/bee-core/src/lock.rs, never reimplement. search supports --tag / --scope / OR-ranked multi-term --text / --all over the archive; reproduce each ranking comparator at its own call site rather than unifying them. REVIEW-FOUND FIXTURE GAP: `queen-bench --generate` produces monotone filler — every decisions row is type `decide` with an identical date, no tags, and there are no supersede or redact rows (crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs:287), and no .bee/decisions-archive.jsonl at all. Every scenario below is therefore non-discriminating unless it SEEDS what it asserts, using the per-scenario seeding rpl-1 provides on top of the baseline store. Register --cmd-check scenarios: search across every filter incl. a multi-term text query whose ranking separates candidates; search --tag over seeded tags; archive with the store at and past its threshold, with a seeded archive sidecar; tag on a missing id; active with seeded superseded AND redacted entries present; and this group's unknown-verb usage fallback line (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609). TWO ITEMS CARRIED FROM THE rpl-4 GOAL-CHECK, both in this group and both owed here. (1) COMPOSED-HANDLER GAP. rpl-4's sweep-with-hits path had its two COMPONENTS oracle-compared, but the composed handler was not: crates/queen-bee/src/ledger/decisions.rs:272-293 (the per-hit capture-stub loop) and :295-313 (the `Propagation sweep: N citation(s)` header plus the two-space-indented `{file}:{line}  {excerpt}` hit lines) have no oracle test and no --cmd-check scenario. A reviewer read them against packages/bee/bee.mjs:1975-1992 and they matched textually, but a read is not an executed assertion. Close it here: the sweep-with-hits output cannot go through --cmd-check (the fresh event uuid sits as an ARRAY ELEMENT under dids and inside outcome prose, which normalize.rs's key-gated deny-by-default masking cannot reach, and widening it to pattern masking would blind rpl-3's capture surface), so add an ORACLE test that drives the composed handler on both runtimes over a docs tree with real citation hits and compares stdout plus the resulting capture-queue rows against the frozen mjs. (2) UTF-16 INCONSISTENCY. crates/bee-core/src/decisions.rs:869 computes short8 as target_id.chars().take(8) — SCALAR VALUES — while packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:465 uses targetId.slice(0, 8) — UTF-16 CODE UNITS. Unreachable for uuids but reachable in principle, since supersede accepts an arbitrary id (the conformance suite itself uses a non-uuid). The same file already handles this correctly in js_excerpt, so it is an inconsistency, not an unknown: make short8 use the same code-unit helper and pin it with an astral-character case.

truths: cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group decisions reports every decisions query scenario clean, mjs vs queen-bee
each scenario SEEDS the rows it asserts on (superseded, redacted, tagged, archived) rather than relying on the monotone baseline store
multi-term --text ranking order matches mjs on a query designed to separate candidates
archive behaves identically at and past the threshold, with the archive sidecar byte-identical
the decisions unknown-verb usage fallback line is byte-identical to mjs

the workspace test run at the head of this cell verify is green with --no-fail-fast, so no cross-cutting pin has rotted outside every cell own gate (the rpl-3 goal-check found one that had been false for two cells because it sat outside every verify and was never executed)

the composed sweep-with-hits handler path (ledger/decisions.rs stub loop plus the Propagation sweep header and hit lines) is compared against the frozen mjs by an executed oracle test, not by a reading
short8 counts UTF-16 code units like mjs slice(0,8), pinned by a supersede target id whose first 8 code units contain an astral character

artifacts.substantive: active projection, search ranking comparators, archive, tag
decisions query verbs behind the rpl-1 seam
decisions query scenarios with their own seeding

key_links: rpl-8's feedback aggregator reads .bee/decisions.jsonl and depends on this projection being byte-right
the D9 lock consumed here is the same one rpl-4 wired
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No unification of the per-call-site ranking comparators
No index rendering in this cell — that is rpl-10
No clean-diff acceptance over the unseeded monotone baseline store
No widening normalize.rs to pattern masking to force the sweep-with-hits path through --cmd-check — that would blind the capture surface rpl-3 built

verify: cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml --workspace --no-fail-fast && cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group decisions

trace.outcome: Ported the decisions QUERY verbs (active, search, archive, tag) behind the rpl-1 seam, byte-identical to the frozen mjs; render deliberately left to rpl-10. Closed both rpl-4 goal-check gaps: the composed sweep-with-hits handler now has an executed two-runtime oracle test, and short8 now measures UTF-16 code units like slice(0,8) instead of scalar values, pinned by an astral-id case where the two readings are mutually exclusive. 21 new --cmd-check scenarios, each seeding the rows it asserts on because the generated fixture is monotone filler; the harness rejected four non-discriminating controls along the way. Added bee_core::jsdate::date_parse_ms for the user-supplied --before/--since arguments, with two V8 behaviours declared rather than reproduced (decision a6c73472).
